canonical.name: The design prose lists the local-compactness theorem before Riesz's lemma, but the manifest reverses them because the theorem's infinite-dimensional direction genuinely uses Riesz's lemma.
The countable-Hamel-basis theorem is scaffolded with the sharper separable-complete Baire route, not by citing the already-published DC-equivalent complete-metric Baire theorem.

The existing draft recorded-not-proved remarks rem-banach-no-countable-hamel-basis and rem-kuratowski-wojdyslawski overlap this page's theorem items, but the batch keeps new theorem ids because those earlier records are not the authored, proved-here versions that this page needs.

The design's B-page choice-strength remark cannot reuse the existing draft item id rem-discontinuous-functional-choice-strength because future-batch manifests may not mint already-authored ids; the batch therefore keeps the design's fresh remark id and records the duplicate explicitly in notes.

sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis
sources.locator: Contents on PDF pp. iii-v; Section 1.5 "Compactness" on printed pp. 24-25 (PDF pp. 36-37), including the total-boundedness bullets, the standard-basis-vector example in ell^p(N), and Theorem 1.11; and the end of Section 4.2 "The Hahn-Banach theorem and its consequences" on printed pp. 127-128 (PDF pp. 139-140), especially Corollary 4.18 and the immediately preceding norm-one separation consequence.

contents.name: Section 1.5, Compactness
the bullet list: relatively compact iff every sequence has a convergent subsequence iff the set is totally bounded
Example, the standard basis vectors in ell^p(N) admit no convergent subsequence
Theorem 1.11, the closed unit ball in a Banach space is compact if and only if the space is finite-dimensional
the norm-one separation consequence immediately preceding Corollary 4.18
contents.reason: Teschl derives this consequence from Hahn-Banach. The FA-3 design explicitly forbids using Hahn-Banach here, so the separation-functional route stays with FA-4 rather than replacing the Riesz-lemma proof spine.

contents.name: Corollary 4.18, x lies in Y iff every functional vanishing on Y also vanishes at x
contents.reason: This is a Hahn-Banach corollary about annihilating functionals. It belongs to the later dual-space and extension page, not to the pre-Hahn-Banach finite-dimensional page.

the remark that closed and bounded is not enough in general Hilbert spaces, with the orthonormal-basis vectors in ell^2 as witness

contents.name: Abstract claim: Mazur's Lemma is provable in ZF
Abstract claim: a real normed vector space is finite-dimensional if and only if its closed unit ball is compact, and this is provable in ZF
Abstract claim: no infinite-dimensional Banach space can be written as a denumerable union of finite-dimensional subspaces lies in strength between AC_omega and AC_fin^omega
Abstract claim: DC implies no infinite-dimensional Banach space can be written as a denumerable union of closed proper subspaces
Abstract claim: every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a well-orderable Hamel basis is equivalent to AC
contents.reason: The page only needs the countably infinite and denumerable-union consequences plus the choice-cost warning. The stronger equivalence with full choice belongs to the library's dedicated choice-ledger remarks rather than to this functional-analysis pair.
